Our jobs aren’t just about giving guests a clean room and a freshly made bed. Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique. Our Guest Environment Experts are skilled in a wide range of housekeeping functions with responsibility for maintaining the appearance and cleanliness of the whole hotel. They are empowered to move about their space and do what needs to be done. Whether delivering guest requests, stocking carts, cleaning rooms and public spaces, or other similar responsibilities, the Guest Environment Expert makes sure the spaces in the hotel help create a great guest experience.

No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – ensuring a safe work place, following company policies and procedures, maintaining confidentiality, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Guest Environment Experts will be on their feet and moving around (stand, sit, or walk for an extended time) and taking a hands-on approach to work (move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 50 pounds without assistance). Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for Guest Environment Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time.

The Human Resources Manager leads the full people function for the ambulatory surgery center in Dubai. The role builds and retains a licensed, high-performing clinical and administrative workforce, ensures compliance with UAE labor law and Dubai Health Authority (DHA) requirements, and acts as a trusted adviser to center leadership on talent, culture, and employee relations.
Develop and execute recruitment plans for surgeons, anesthesiologists, nurses, operating theatre technicians, allied health, and administrative staff.
Manage sourcing, interviewing, offers, and visa, labor card, and Emirates ID processing for new hires.
Coordinate DHA licensing, primary source verification, and credentialing with the Medical Director and Quality department.
Run structured onboarding and orientation, including infection control, patient safety, and competency sign-off.
Serve as the first point of contact for employee concerns; investigate and resolve grievances and disciplinary matters fairly and confidentially.
Promote a culture of patient safety, respect, and teamwork across clinical and non-clinical teams.
Lead engagement, recognition, and retention initiatives and monitor turnover and satisfaction indicators.
Administer salary structures, allowances, medical insurance, annual leave, airfare, and end-of-service entitlements in line with UAE Labour Law.
Work with Finance to prepare payroll inputs, the Wage Protection System (WPS) process, and the annual manpower budget.
Benchmark compensation against the Dubai healthcare market and recommend adjustments.
Forecast staffing needs based on surgical case volumes, theatre schedules, and service line growth.
Partner with the Director of Nursing and department heads on rosters, relief cover, and overtime control within working-time rules.
Maintain accurate headcount, vacancy, and cost reporting for leadership.
Manage annual performance appraisals, goal setting, and succession planning.
Coordinate mandatory training and continuing professional development, including BLS/ACLS and license renewals.
Track clinical competency and training compliance for accreditation readiness.
Ensure compliance with UAE Labour Law, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) regulations, DHA requirements, and applicable Joint Commission International (JCI) standards.
Maintain personnel files, licence and visa expiry tracking, and audit-ready HR records.
Develop, update, and communicate HR policies and procedures.
Manage Emiratisation targets and reporting, and protect employee data and confidentiality.
